variants.headline: Looking back: new settlers land from the ship
variants.sub: The ship in port has brought new settlers who landed at {district}.
variants.body:
We return to our earlier coverage. Our report recorded this: New settlers have landed from the ship at {district}.

The gazette records the number of arrivals and the place where the settlers landed. Arrival and subsequent settlement arrangements are distinct matters. Administrative clarity should preserve that distinction while recognising the newcomers as people whose place in the colony cannot be fully described by the act of disembarking.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We welcome {target} in this assessment. Receiving new settlers deserves a fair hearing and recognition of the human connection involved, without requiring invented achievements about the lives that follow their arrival.

variants.headline: Looking back: an arrival becomes a colonial beginning
variants.sub: The district {district} has received new settlers landing from the ship.
